sample_unit: LLM-generated texts (20 per model, 20 per theme)

links.outcome: Readability and patient-education appropriateness of LLM texts on gestational hypertension
links.effect: GPT-5 highest C-PEMAT (11.10 ± 2.40); readability varied by content category, with etiology and risk factor texts showing weaker reading fluency; quality and readability largely independent.
links.quote: Content categories exhibited differentiated readability but stable quality: texts on "Prevention and Prognosis" and "Treatment and Management" yielded the highest C-PEMAT scores, whereas "Etiology and Risk Factors" texts showed weaker reading fluency.

links.outcome: Factual accuracy of LLM responses on gestational hypertension
links.effect: 19.0% of responses contained factual inaccuracies; none judged potentially clinically harmful; significant between-model differences in factual accuracy scores.
links.quote: In the factual-accuracy assessment, 19.0% of responses contained factual inaccuracies, while no response was judged to contain potentially clinically harmful misinformation.

screen.reason: Evaluates and benchmarks multiple commercial LLMs on quality, readability, and factual accuracy for gestational hypertension patient education FAQs without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
